issues.description: An exact prepared Glassdoor review/GVKEY route is required, but current local entitlement and input compatibility are unknown. The NDA establishes a public-sharing restriction only; the frozen catalog miss does not establish absent access.

Active stages consume three distinct author-prepared RavenPack extracts. A hash-bound lexical review confirms that Stage 05 lines 20–142 and Stage 06 lines 23–77 contain candidate producer code entirely inside SAS `/*...*/` block comments, with no active statements in those ranges. The supplied commented construction and filters reference candidate interfaces including rpna.rp_entity_mapping and rpna.rp_equities_2012; the official SAS comment reference confirms that this comment form hides contents from macro processing, so its in-span macro include and triggers do not activate a producer in the current files. This code is supplied as candidate construction, but compatibility of its supplied filters and fields with the local product, the intended PERMNO mapping, the schemas expected by downstream consumers, and 2012–2018 versus 2012–2016 coverage remains unverified. Catalog candidates and bounded local reads do not establish those contracts.

Stage 07 actively merges Data/tempchgemp.dta by GVKEY/fiscal year. Supplied Stage 05 instead exports PercentageChangeEmp.dta (GVKEY, DATADATE, FYEAR, pct_chng_emp) and employee_lag.dta; neither is proven to be the named input.

Stage 01 uses current-directory-relative paths; SAS roots/macros are blank or unresolved; Stage 07 derives Data/Rawdata/Program from an empty root global; producers and consumers use different configured roots; and Stage 04 exports fqtr.dta while Stage 07 imports FQTR.dta. Configure exact cross-language handoffs and case on the host filesystem.

The supplied SAS stages use library and root bindings that need host-specific values for a later run. Set those ordinary path/configuration values in a separate portable working copy; choosing the local physical roots does not require the authors' original paths or approval. Protected statement bodies remain omitted from this assessment. SAS runtime and each data product's access/field/history contracts are assessed separately.

SAS 9.4 Base is required for the supplied SAS stages; its availability in the intended batch environment remains unverified. The prior TKELS initialization failure is retained only as limited process history and does not establish absence of SAS or a license barrier.
